penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Physical infrastructure audits require on-site or at minimum deeply contextual human judgment to validate — a checklist SaaS alone is insufficient for the actual audit deliverable buyers expect.

penalties_applied.name: high_touch_support
penalties_applied.reason: Datacenter ops managers will require explanations and customization of audit findings, creating ongoing support load per customer.

rationale: The buyer is real (datacenter ops managers at SMB colos) and the pain is genuine, but the core deliverable — a meaningful physical infrastructure audit — requires human expertise and on-site judgment that Claude cannot replace; a pure checklist SaaS would not satisfy buyers with active SLA obligations. Operational autonomy is low (each engagement requires human-in-the-loop fulfillment), and the signal is a single anecdote from a Jane Street incident, with no tested responsiveness. The penalties pull the total below the validate threshold.
solution_plan: This opportunity is not viable as a solo non-technical factory-run service. A credible physical infrastructure audit requires domain experts who can evaluate fuel supply chains, cooling layouts, and flood mitigation — Claude can generate a checklist, but buyers with 99.9%+ SLA obligations will not pay for an unvalidated AI-generated checklist alone. The operator (Youval) would need to hire or partner with datacenter engineers to deliver actual value, which exceeds the solo+Claude model. Drop and monitor for a narrower, software-only angle (e.g., SLA documentation review or vendor contract analysis) where Claude can deliver autonomously.
notes: Failing build_gates: operational_autonomy (4 < 7 required). The human fulfillment penalty is structural, not incidental.
